ESV.1: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
ESV.2: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to entreat the favor of the LORD,
ESV.3: saying to the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts and the prophets, “Should I weep and abstain in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?”
ESV.4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
ESV.5: “Say to all the people of the land and the priests, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh, for these seventy years, was it for me that you fasted?
ESV.6: And when you eat and when you drink, do you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves?
ESV.7: Were not these the words that the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, with her cities around her, and the South and the lowland were inhabited?’”
ESV.8: And the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,
ESV.9: “Thus says the LORD of hosts, Render true judgments, show kindness and mercy to one another,
ESV.10: do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner, or the poor, and let none of you devise evil against another in your heart.”
ESV.11: But they refused to pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears that they might not hear.
ESV.12: They made their hearts diamond-hard lest they should hear the law and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by his Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great anger came from the LORD of hosts.
ESV.13: “As I  called, and they would not hear, so they called, and I would not hear,” says the LORD of hosts,
ESV.14: “and I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known. Thus the land they left was desolate, so that no one went to and fro, and the pleasant land was made desolate.”

NKJV.1: Now in the fourth year of King Darius it came to pass that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chislev,
NKJV.2: when the people sent Sherezer, with Regem-Melech and his men, to the house of God, to pray before the LORD,
NKJV.3: and to ask the priests who were in the house of the LORD of hosts, and the prophets, saying, “Should I weep in the fifth month and fast as I have done for so many years?”
NKJV.4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,
NKJV.5: “Say to all the people of the land, and to the priests: ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months during those seventy years, did you really fast for Me—for Me?
NKJV.6: When you eat and when you drink, do you not eat and drink for yourselves?
NKJV.7: Should you not have obeyed the words which the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets when Jerusalem and the cities around it were inhabited and prosperous, and the South and the Lowland were inhabited?’ ”
NKJV.8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,
NKJV.9: “Thus says the LORD of hosts:  ‘Execute true justice, Show mercy and compassion Everyone to his brother.
NKJV.10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, The alien or the poor.  Let none of you plan evil in his heart Against his brother.’
NKJV.11: “But they refused to heed, shrugged their shoulders, and stopped their ears so that they could not hear.
NKJV.12: Yes, they made their hearts like flint, refusing to hear the law and the words which the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Thus great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
NKJV.13: Therefore it happened, that just as He proclaimed and they would not hear, so they called out and I would not listen,” says the LORD of hosts.
NKJV.14: “But I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they had not known. Thus the land became desolate after them, so that no one passed through or returned; for they made the pleasant land desolate.”

NASB.1: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth [day] of the ninth month, [which is] Chislev.
NASB.2: Now [the town of] Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regemmelech and their men to seek the favor of the LORD,
NASB.3: speaking to the priests who belong to the house of the LORD of hosts, and to the prophets, saying, 'Shall I weep in the fifth month and abstain, as I have done these many years?'
NASB.4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,
NASB.5: 'Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years, was it actually for Me that you fasted?
NASB.6: 'When you eat and drink, do you not eat for yourselves and do you not drink for yourselves?
NASB.7: 'Are not [these] the words which the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous along with its cities around it, and the Negev and the foothills were inhabited?''
NASB.8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah saying,
NASB.9: 'Thus has the LORD of hosts said, 'Dispense true justice and practice kindness and compassion each to his brother;
NASB.10: and do not oppress the widow or the orphan, the stranger or the poor; and do not devise evil in your hearts against one another.'
NASB.11: 'But they refused to pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears from hearing.
NASB.12: 'They made their hearts [like] flint so that they could not hear the law and the words which the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets; therefore great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
NASB.13: 'And just as He called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen,' says the LORD of hosts;
NASB.14: 'but I scattered them with a storm wind among all the nations whom they have not known. Thus the land is desolated behind them so that no one went back and forth, for they made the pleasant land desolate.'

WEB.1: In the fourth year of king Darius, Yahweh’s word came to Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev.
WEB.2: The people of Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem Melech, and their men, to entreat Yahweh’s favor,
WEB.3: and to speak to the priests of the house of Yahweh of Armies, and to the prophets, saying, “Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?”
WEB.4: Then the word of Yahweh of Armies came to me, saying,
WEB.5: “Speak to all the people of the land, and to the priests, saying, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month for these seventy years, did you at all fast to me, really to me?
WEB.6: When you eat, and when you drink, don’t you eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?
WEB.7: Aren’t these the words which Yahweh proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and its cities around her, and the South and the lowland were inhabited?’”
WEB.8: Yahweh’s word came to Zechariah, saying,
WEB.9: “Thus has Yahweh of Armies spoken, saying, ‘Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother.
WEB.10: Don’t oppress the widow, nor the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.’
WEB.11: But they refused to listen, and turned their backs, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear.
WEB.12: Yes, they made their hearts as hard as flint, lest they might hear the law, and the words which Yahweh of Armies had sent by his Spirit by the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from Yahweh of Armies.
WEB.13: It has come to pass that, as he called, and they refused to listen, so they will call, and I will not listen,” said Yahweh of Armies;
WEB.14: “but I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they have not known. Thus the land was desolate after them, so that no man passed through nor returned: for they made the pleasant land desolate.”

AMP.1: In the fourth year of [the reign of] King Darius [of Persia], the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev (Dec 7, 518 b.c.).
AMP.2: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to seek the favor of the LORD,
AMP.3: speaking to the priests who belong to the house of the LORD of hosts and to the prophets, saying, "[Now that I am returned from exile] shall I weep in the fifth month [mourning the destruction of the temple], and fast as I have done these many years [in Babylon]?"
AMP.4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me (Zechariah), saying,
AMP.5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years [that you were in exile], was it actually for Me that you fasted?
AMP.6: When you eat and when you drink, do you not eat for yourselves and do you not drink for yourselves [to satisfy your own needs]?
AMP.7: Should you not hear the words which the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous along with her cities around her, and the South (the Negev) and the foothills were inhabited?'"
AMP.8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,
AMP.9: "Thus has the LORD of hosts said, 'Dispense true justice and practice kindness and compassion, to each other;
AMP.10: and do not oppress or exploit the widow or the fatherless, the stranger or the poor; and do not devise or even imagine evil in your hearts against one another.'
AMP.11: But they refused to listen and pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder [stiffening themselves in resistance] and stopped up their ears.
AMP.12: They made their hearts [hard] like flint, so that they could not hear the law and the words which the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
AMP.13: And just as He called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen," says the LORD of hosts;
AMP.14: "but I scattered them with a storm wind among all the nations whom they have not known. Thus the land was desolate after they had gone, so that no one passed through or returned, for they [by their sins] had made the pleasant land desolate and deserted.'"

CSB17.1: In the fourth year of King Darius, <sup>ⓒ</sup> the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
CSB17.2: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer, Regem-melech, and their men to plead for the LORD’s favor <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.3: by asking the priests who were at the house of the LORD of Armies as well as the prophets, “Should we mourn and fast in the fifth month as we have done these many years?”
CSB17.4: Then the word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
CSB17.5: “Ask all the people of the land and the priests: When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and in the seventh months for these seventy years, did you really fast for me? <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.6: When you eat and drink, don’t you eat and drink simply for yourselves? <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.7: Aren’t these the words that the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and secure, <sup>[1]</sup> along with its surrounding cities, and when the southern region and the Judean foothills were inhabited?”
CSB17.8: The word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
CSB17.9: “The LORD of Armies says this: ‘Make fair decisions. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Show faithful love and compassion <sup>ⓗ</sup> to one another.
CSB17.10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the resident alien or the poor, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and do not plot evil in your hearts against one another.’ <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.11: But they refused to pay attention <sup>ⓚ</sup> and turned a stubborn shoulder; they closed their ears so they could not hear. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.12: They made their hearts like a rock so as not to obey the law or the words that the LORD of Armies had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. <sup>ⓜ</sup> Therefore intense anger came from the LORD of Armies.
CSB17.13: Just as he had called, and they would not listen, so when they called, I would not listen, says the LORD of Armies.
CSB17.14: I scattered them with a windstorm over all the nations that had not known them, and the land was left desolate behind them, with no one coming or going. They turned a pleasant land into a desolation.”

NLT.1: On December 7 of the fourth year of King Darius’s reign, another message came to Zechariah from the LORD.
NLT.2: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regemmelech, along with their attendants, to seek the LORD’s favor.
NLT.3: They were to ask this question of the prophets and the priests at the Temple of the LORD of Heaven’s Armies: “Should we continue to mourn and fast each summer on the anniversary of the Temple’s destruction, as we have done for so many years?”
NLT.4: The LORD of Heaven’s Armies sent me this message in reply:
NLT.5: “Say to all your people and your priests, ‘During these seventy years of exile, when you fasted and mourned in the summer and in early autumn, was it really for me that you were fasting?
NLT.6: And even now in your holy festivals, aren’t you eating and drinking just to please yourselves?
NLT.7: Isn’t this the same message the LORD proclaimed through the prophets in years past when Jerusalem and the towns of Judah were bustling with people, and the Negev and the foothills of Judah were well populated?’”
NLT.8: Then this message came to Zechariah from the LORD:
NLT.9: “This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: Judge fairly, and show mercy and kindness to one another.
NLT.10: Do not oppress widows, orphans, foreigners, and the poor. And do not scheme against each other.
NLT.11: “Your ancestors refused to listen to this message. They stubbornly turned away and put their fingers in their ears to keep from hearing.
NLT.12: They made their hearts as hard as stone, so they could not hear the instructions or the messages that the LORD of Heaven’s Armies had sent them by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. That is why the LORD of Heaven’s Armies was so angry with them.
NLT.13: “Since they refused to listen when I called to them, I would not listen when they called to me, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
NLT.14: As with a whirlwind, I scattered them among the distant nations, where they lived as strangers. Their land became so desolate that no one even traveled through it. They turned their pleasant land into a desert.”

NET.1: In King Darius’ fourth year, on the fourth day of Kislev, the ninth month, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah.
NET.2: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and their companions to seek the LORD’s favor
NET.3: by asking both the priests of the temple of the LORD WHO RULES OVER ALL and the prophets, “Should we weep in the fifth month, fasting as we have done over the years?”
NET.4: The word of the LORD who rules over all then came to me,
NET.5: “Speak to all the people and priests of the land as follows: ‘When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and seventh months through all these seventy years, did you truly fast for me — for me, indeed?
NET.6: And now when you eat and drink, are you not doing so for yourselves?’”
NET.7: Should you not have obeyed the words that the LORD cried out through the former prophets when Jerusalem was peacefully inhabited and her surrounding cities, the Negev, and the Shephelah were also populated?
NET.8: Again the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
NET.9: “The LORD who rules over all said, ‘Exercise true judgment and show brotherhood and compassion to each other.
NET.10: You must not oppress the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, or the poor, nor should anyone secretly plot evil against his fellow human being.’
NET.11: “But they refused to pay attention, turning away stubbornly and stopping their ears so they could not hear.
NET.12: Indeed, they made their heart as hard as diamond, so that they could not obey the Torah and the other words the LORD who rules over all had sent by his Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore, the LORD who rules over all had poured out great wrath.
NET.13: “‘It then came about that just as I cried out, but they would not obey, so they will cry out, but I will not listen,’ the LORD LORD WHO RULES OVER ALL had said.
NET.14: ‘Rather, I will sweep them away in a storm into all the nations they are not familiar with.’ Thus the land had become desolate because of them, with no one crossing through or returning, for they had made the fruitful land a waste.”

NIV.1:
Justice and Mercy, Not Fasting
In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Kislev.
NIV.2: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech, together with their men, to entreat the Lord
NIV.3: by asking the priests of the house of the Lord Almighty and the prophets, “Should I mourn and fast in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?”
NIV.4: Then the word of the Lord Almighty came to me:
NIV.5: “Ask all the people of the land and the priests, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for the past seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
NIV.6: And when you were eating and drinking, were you not just feasting for yourselves?
NIV.7: Are these not the words the Lord proclaimed through the earlier prophets when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were at rest and prosperous, and the Negev and the western foothills were settled?’”
NIV.8: And the word of the Lord came again to Zechariah:
NIV.9: “This is what the Lord Almighty says: ‘Administer true justice; show mercy and compassion to one another.
NIV.10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the alien or the poor. In your hearts do not think evil of each other.’
NIV.11: “But they refused to pay attention; stubbornly they turned their backs and stopped up their ears.
NIV.12: They made their hearts as hard as flint and would not listen to the law or to the words that the Lord Almighty had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So the Lord Almighty was very angry.
NIV.13: “‘When I called, they did not listen; so when they called, I would not listen,’ says the Lord Almighty.
NIV.14: ‘I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations, where they were strangers. The land was left so desolate behind them that no one could come or go. This is how they made the pleasant land desolate.’”
